    Erisian Standard¶

    [!INFO] The Empire's Yardstick — One Foot to Rule Them The bureaucratic measure of the Erisian Empire — cut from the Emperor's own foot, copied in iron, and nailed to every tollhouse from Central Erisdar to the South Erisdar border.

    Base Units¶

    The Standard was decreed under Hermes Kennensbach's predecessors and re-certified in 432 AGD against a platinum-iridium bar kept in the Imperial Vault at Erisgard. All provincial copies must be re-stamped every seven years by the Pontificate — a tax in itself.

    Domain Unit Relation Notes
    Length Grain base 1 barley grain, lengthwise
    Finger 4 Grains digitus — for cloth
    Palm 4 Fingers hand-breadth
    Inch 3 Grains uncia — thumb-joint
    Foot 12 Inches pes — the Emperor's foot, 30.48 cm
    Ell 18 Inches forearm — taxable cloth width
    Yard 3 Feet pace of a guardsman
    Rod 16.5 Feet surveyor's rod — field measure
    Chain 4 Rods 66 Feet — 100 Chains = 1 Furlong
    Furlong 40 Rods furrow-long — agrarian standard
    Mile 8 Furlongs 5,280 Feet — 1,000 double-steps of the legion
    Weight Grain base 1 barley grain, weight
    Pennyweight 24 Grains assay weight
    Ounce 20 Pennyweights uncia
    Pound 16 Ounces libra — 453.6 g. Tax pound
    Stone 14 Pounds for bodies, wool, and conscripts
    Hundredweight 8 Stone 112 Pounds
    Ton 20 Hundredweight 2,240 Pounds — long ton
    Volume Pint base 0.57 L
    Quart 2 Pints
    Gallon 8 Pints 4.54 L — wine & oil
    Bushel 8 Gallons dry — grain tithe
    Tun 252 Gallons great cask — cellar measure

    Provincial cheat: the Loren Yard is 1.02 Erisian Yards. The Imperial Exchequer knows and charges accordingly.

    Who Uses¶

    Dominant across Central Erisdar — Erisian Empire, Pontificate of Eris, Erisian Theocracy, Archduchy of the Kennberg, Loren, Magna, New Baoth, Sperdia, and the Imperial subdivisions (38 counties, 4 free cities). Also the lingua franca for contracts in South Erisdar when neither party trusts Anosi nor Vennerian paper.

    Clerks, taxmen, legion quartermasters, and cathedral builders. Every bridge arch in the Empire is 2 Rods wide because the manual says so.

    Conversion Notes¶

    • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Erisian Foot = 0.97 Dwarven Stone-Foot. Dwarves call the Imperial Foot long and lazy. 1 Erisian Pound = 0.98 Dwarven Pound — close enough to argue over at every border market in Dwarvengor.
    • To Vennerian Cable: 1 Erisian Mile = 0.87 Vennerian Nautical Miles. Vennerian factors quote sea distance in Cables; Erisian caravans stamp it back to Miles and pocket the rounding.
    • To Anosi Ledger-Weight: Numerically identical — Anos deliberately shadowed the Imperial table so merchants would not need two sets of weights. Difference is legal, not metrical: Anosi weights are certified by counting-houses, Erisian by the Vault.
    • To Mann Star-Stride: 1 Mann Star-Stride ≈ 1,000 Erisian Yards. Mann priests refuse the Mile as southern vanity.
    • Romanium clause: Romanium dust is weighed in Erisian Grains for Imperial assay. Anos and Venner both accept the Erisian Grain for Romanium — the one thing all three agree on.

    Flavor¶

    The Standard is not loved — it is obeyed. A farmer in Magna knows his field is 12 Chains by 8 because the countisman measured it with an iron Chain that has not changed since his grandfather's grandfather, and the tithe is 3 Bushels per Furlong because the parchment says so. The iron Foot in its shrine at Erisgard is kissed by new magistrates. To file it down is treason; to lose it is comedy for the Exchequer.

    Anos joke: Venner measures the sea, dwarves measure stone, the Empire measures its own virtue — and finds itself exactly one Mile magnificent.
